region: Tropical Americas: Mexico, Central and South America, Caribbean
description: Genuine mahogany comes from Swietenia trees, chiefly big-leaf or Honduran mahogany (S. macrophylla) and the now scarce Cuban or West Indian mahogany (S. mahagoni). It is a stable, easily worked reddish-brown hardwood long prized for fine furniture, cabinetry, boat building and guitar bodies.

hazards.summary: Skin rashes are reported in people who work mahogany, and a UK agency lists dermatitis among its effects. A case report describes work-related dermatitis from Honduran mahogany, and a Finnish clinic recorded positive patch tests to a wood sold as mahogany.
The UK safety regulator lists breathing problems and irritation of the nose, throat and eyes among the reported effects of mahogany dust.
Occupational asthma from American mahogany (S. mahagoni) is listed in a peer-reviewed review of wood dust allergy, based on a German workplace study we have not yet been able to check directly.
ACGIH names mahogany dust as a suspected human carcinogen (class A2). The listing does not say which botanical mahogany is meant; we apply it to genuine Swietenia mahogany.
IARC classifies all wood dust as carcinogenic to humans, mainly linked to cancers of the nasal cavity and sinuses after long-term exposure.

related_species_note: Many unrelated timbers are sold as 'mahogany', including African mahogany (Khaya), sapele (Entandrophragma) and Philippine mahogany or lauan (Shorea and related genera). Hazard evidence for those woods is listed on their own pages.
image_prompt: Photorealistic studio photograph of a freshly planed genuine mahogany (Swietenia macrophylla) board, shot at a low three-quarter angle so the face grain fills most of the frame. Heartwood a warm medium reddish-brown with salmon-pink tones on the fresh surface, deepening toward rich red-brown; a narrow edge of pale yellowish-white sapwood along one side. Straight to slightly interlocked grain with a faint ribbon stripe, medium even texture, small open pores visible as fine dark flecks along the grain, and a soft golden shimmer (chatoyance) where the light catches the face. Soft diffused daylight from upper left, gentle falloff, neutral warm-grey seamless background, shallow depth of field with the near edge tack-sharp. No text, no logos, no hands, no tools, no finish or varnish, natural unfinished wood. Wide 1200x630 composition (1.91:1) with the board centered and margin on both sides for cropping.
image_alt: Planed board of genuine mahogany with warm reddish-brown heartwood, a faint ribbon stripe and a thin edge of pale sapwood.
notes_internal: Sosman-1969 (seed lead) is verified as a citation (PMID 4980984) but has no abstract and the full text is paywalled, so we could not confirm it involves mahogany or what testing was done; it is defined in the batch sources but not cited on any hazard. The asthma entry rests on Schlunssen-2018 Table 1 (S. mahagoni, citing Kersten & von Wahl 1994, Allergologie 17:55-60, not indexed in PubMed). HSE-WIS30 lists 'Mahogany' without a botanical name; it is applied here per the handoff seed list but may refer to Khaya as well. Estlander-2001 patch-test reactions were to 'mahogany' without botanical identification. ACGIH A2 'mahogany' is unspecified botanically (OSHA page checked 2026-11-07); another agent is resolving this. Fowler-1985 has no abstract; testing method unconfirmed.
